practiceQuestions.q: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word in the sentence: 'She behaved in a very friendly manner.'
practiceQuestions.sol: Although 'friendly' ends in '-ly', it modifies the noun 'manner'. Therefore, it functions as an Adjective. Words like friendly, lovely, and silly are adjectives, not adverbs.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'He went up the hill,' what is the part of speech of the word 'up'?
practiceQuestions.sol: In this sentence, 'up' is followed by the noun phrase 'the hill' (its object), which establishes a spatial relationship. Therefore, it functions as a Preposition.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the word class of 'up' in the sentence: 'The prices are going up.'
practiceQuestions.sol: Here, 'up' modifies the verb 'going' and does not take an object. Therefore, it functions as an Adverb of direction.

practiceQuestions.q: Which part of speech is the word 'crying' in the phrase: 'a crying baby'?
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Crying' modifies the noun 'baby' and functions as a verbal adjective, which is a Present Participle.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'Swimming is a healthy exercise,' what category does 'Swimming' belong to?
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Swimming' is a verb form ending in -ing that acts as the subject of the sentence, which means it functions as a verbal noun or Gerund.

practiceQuestions.q: Choose the sentence that contains a relative pronoun:
opts: I know that he is honest.
This is the book that I lost yesterday.
practiceQuestions.sol: In the second sentence, 'that' refers back to 'the book' and introduces the relative clause 'I lost yesterday'. Hence, it is a Relative Pronoun.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: 'He walked fast to catch the bus.'
practiceQuestions.sol: Here, 'fast' modifies the action verb 'walked', describing how he walked. Therefore, it is an Adverb.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'He is a fast runner,' what is the part of speech of 'fast'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Here, 'fast' modifies the noun 'runner'. Hence, it functions as an Adjective.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the relative pronoun in the following options:
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Who' is a relative pronoun used to refer to people. 'Him' is a personal pronoun, 'Myself' is reflexive, and 'Each' is indefinite.

practiceQuestions.q: Which category of conjunction does 'neither...nor' belong to?
practiceQuestions.sol: Conjunctions that are used in pairs, like 'neither...nor' and 'either...or', are classified as Correlative Conjunctions.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'She herself went to see the patient,' the word 'herself' is a/an:
practiceQuestions.sol: When reflexive pronouns (like herself, himself, myself) are used immediately after a noun or pronoun to add emphasis, they function as Emphatic Pronouns.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'She hurt herself,' the word 'herself' is a/an:
practiceQuestions.sol: In this sentence, the action of the verb 'hurt' reflects back to the subject 'She'. Thus, 'herself' is the object of the verb and functions as a Reflexive Pronoun.

practiceQuestions.q: In the phrase: 'Those mangoes are ripe,' the word 'Those' is a/an:
practiceQuestions.sol: Since 'Those' immediately precedes and modifies the noun 'mangoes', it functions as a Demonstrative Adjective. If it stood alone (e.g., 'Those are ripe'), it would be a Demonstrative Pronoun.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the subordinating conjunction in the following sentence: 'We shall not go out if it rains.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'if' is a subordinating conjunction because it introduces the dependent conditional clause 'if it rains'.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the part of speech of the word 'before' in: 'I have seen you before.'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Since 'before' does not have an object here and refers to time, it functions as an Adverb of time.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the part of speech of the word 'before' in: 'He stood before the judge.'?
practiceQuestions.sol: In this sentence, 'before' is followed by the noun phrase 'the judge' (its object), signifying position. Therefore, it is a Preposition.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the collective noun in the sentence: 'The jury was unanimous in its decision.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Jury' represents a group of judges or individuals acting as a single collective unit, making it a Collective Noun.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is an example of an abstract noun?
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Childhood' refers to a state or stage of life which is abstract, whereas 'Gold' is material, 'Team' is collective, and 'London' is proper.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'He is the man whom I met yesterday,' the word 'whom' is a/an:
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Whom' is a Relative Pronoun used in the objective case, connecting the relative clause to the noun 'man'.

practiceQuestions.q: Which part of speech is 'but' in the sentence: 'It is but right to admit our mistake.'?
practiceQuestions.sol: In this context, 'but' means 'only' (it modifies the adjective 'right'). Hence, it functions as an Adverb.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the word class of 'but' in: 'All but John were present.'
practiceQuestions.sol: In this sentence, 'but' means 'except' and links 'John' to the rest of the sentence. Hence, it functions as a Preposition.

practiceQuestions.q: She runs very quickly. What word class is 'very'?
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Very' modifies the adverb 'quickly' by indicating degree. Therefore, it is an Adverb (Adverb of degree).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is a Coordinating Conjunction?
practiceQuestions.sol: 'But' is a coordinating conjunction (part of the FANBOYS mnemonic). The other options are subordinating conjunctions.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the part of speech of 'round' in: 'The Earth moves round the Sun.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'round' is followed by the object 'the Sun', establishing a physical spatial relationship. Therefore, it is a Preposition.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the part of speech of 'round' in: 'The doctor made his daily round.'
practiceQuestions.sol: In this sentence, 'round' is preceded by the possessive adjective 'his' and descriptive adjective 'daily', serving as the direct object of the verb 'made'. Hence, it is a Noun.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'It was a round table,' what is the part of speech of 'round'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Here, 'round' describes the shape of the noun 'table'. Thus, it functions as an Adjective.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following sentences uses 'crying' as a Gerund?
opts: The crying child was comforted by his mother.
Crying is not the solution to this problem.
She was crying because she lost her keys.
I heard someone crying in the hallway.
practiceQuestions.sol: In 'Crying is not the solution...', 'Crying' functions as the noun subject of the sentence, which is the definition of a Gerund.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'Alas! The great leader is no more,' what is the word 'Alas!'?
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Alas!' is an Interjection because it expresses a sudden strong emotion (grief) and is grammatically independent of the rest of the sentence.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the indefinite pronoun in the following sentence: 'Does anyone know the answer?'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'anyone' is an indefinite pronoun because it refers to an unspecified person.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the part of speech of the word 'still' in: 'Still waters run deep.'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Here, 'still' modifies the noun 'waters' by describing its quiet or calm state. Therefore, it is an Adjective.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the part of speech of 'still' in: 'He is still working in that firm.'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Here, 'still' modifies the verb phrase 'is working', describing the continuation of the action. Therefore, it is an Adverb.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the modal auxiliary verb in the sentence: 'You must submit your assignment by tomorrow.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'must' is a modal auxiliary verb that expresses obligation or necessity.

practiceQuestions.q: Which part of speech is the word 'that' in: 'I know that you will pass.'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Here, 'that' is a conjunction linking the independent clause 'I know' with the dependent noun clause 'you will pass'. It does not refer to any preceding noun.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'She not only sang but also danced,' what type of conjunction is used?
practiceQuestions.sol: 'not only...but also' is a correlative conjunction because it is a paired conjunction linking equivalent parts.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the part of speech of the word 'fast' in the phrase: 'He kept a fast for a week.'?
practiceQuestions.sol: In this context, 'fast' refers to the act of abstaining from food. It is preceded by the article 'a', making it a Noun.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'They fast twice a week,' the word 'fast' is a/an:
practiceQuestions.sol: Here, 'fast' is the action being performed by the subject 'They' (abstaining from food). Thus, it functions as a Verb.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the word class of the underlined word: 'The book on the table is mine.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'mine' replaces the noun phrase 'my book' and shows possession without being followed by a noun. Therefore, it is a Possessive Pronoun.

practiceQuestions.q: Which part of speech is 'my' in the sentence: 'This is my book.'?
practiceQuestions.sol: 'my' modifies the noun 'book' directly to show possession. Therefore, it acts as a Possessive Adjective.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'Whom did you invite for the party?', the word 'Whom' is an:
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Whom' is used here to ask a question, and it acts as the object of the verb. Thus, it is an Interrogative Pronoun.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the part of speech of the word 'after' in: 'They arrived shortly after.'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Since 'after' has no noun object following it, it modifies the verb 'arrived' indicating time. Thus, it functions as an Adverb.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the part of speech of 'after' in: 'They arrived after the storm had passed.'?
practiceQuestions.sol: 'after' connects the independent clause 'They arrived' with the dependent clause 'the storm had passed'. Hence, it functions as a Subordinating Conjunction.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'He took a book from the shelf,' the word 'from' is a/an:
practiceQuestions.sol: 'from' establishes the relationship between 'took a book' and 'the shelf'. It functions as a Preposition.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the word class of 'all' in: 'All men are mortal.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'All' modifies the noun 'men' directly. Therefore, it functions as a Limiting Adjective (or determiner).

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the word class of 'all' in: 'All of us were invited.'
practiceQuestions.sol: In this sentence, 'All' stands in place of a noun phrase as the subject of the clause. Thus, it functions as an Indefinite Pronoun.

practiceQuestions.q: Which part of speech is the word 'silently' in: 'She walked silently through the corridor.'?
practiceQuestions.sol: 'silently' describes how the action 'walked' was performed, making it an Adverb of manner.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'The iron is hot,' the word 'hot' is a/an:
practiceQuestions.sol: 'hot' describes the state of the noun 'iron' and is placed after the linking verb 'is' (predicative use). Thus, it is an Adjective.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the part of speech of the word 'class' in: 'This is a class project.'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Although 'class' is typically a noun, here it is used to modify the noun 'project'. Therefore, it functions as a noun adjunct or Adjective.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'Each of the boys got a prize,' the word 'Each' is a/an:
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Each' stands alone before the prepositional phrase 'of the boys' as the subject. Therefore, it is a Distributive Pronoun.

practiceQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'Each boy got a prize,' the word 'Each' is a/an:
practiceQuestions.sol: Here, 'Each' directly modifies the singular noun 'boy'. Thus, it functions as a Distributive Adjective.

practiceQuestions.q: Identify the conjunction in the sentence: 'Although he worked hard, he failed.'
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction introducing the concessive clause 'Although he worked hard'.

mockTestQuestions.q: Identify the part of speech of 'fast' in: 'He ran as fast as he could.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: In this sentence, 'fast' modifies the action verb 'ran'. Therefore, it is an Adverb.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which part of speech is 'that' in: 'Give me that pen.'?
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'that' directly modifies the noun 'pen' to specify which pen. Hence, it functions as a Demonstrative Adjective.

mockTestQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'The baby cried for its mother,' the word 'its' is a/an:
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'its' modifies the noun 'mother' to show possession. Hence, it is a Possessive Adjective.

mockTestQuestions.q: What is the part of speech of the word 'running' in: 'He bought running shoes.'?
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'running' modifies the noun 'shoes' by describing their purpose/type, acting as a verbal adjective or Present Participle.

mockTestQuestions.q: Identify the type of verb underlined in the sentence: 'She is sleeping peacefully.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: The verb 'sleeping' does not transfer action to any direct object. Thus, it is an Intransitive Verb.

mockTestQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'Either you or he has to go,' what type of conjunction is used?
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'Either...or' works as a pair to connect grammatically coordinate elements, classifying it as a Correlative Conjunction.

mockTestQuestions.q: Identify the relative pronoun in the sentence: 'The dog that barked all night belongs to our neighbor.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'that' relates the dependent clause 'barked all night' back to the noun 'dog', functioning as a Relative Pronoun.

mockTestQuestions.q: What is the word class of 'about' in: 'We talked about our childhood plans.'?
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'about' is followed by the noun phrase object 'our childhood plans', functioning as a Preposition.

mockTestQuestions.q: Identify the word class of 'about' in: 'The train is about to leave.'?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Here, 'about' modifies the infinitive 'to leave' indicating proximity of time. Therefore, it functions as an Adverb.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which part of speech is 'since' in the sentence: 'I have not seen him since we left school.'?
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'since' connects the main clause with the subordinate clausal time modifier 'we left school', functioning as a Subordinating Conjunction.

mockTestQuestions.q: What is the part of speech of the word 'since' in: 'I have not seen him since Monday.'?
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'since' is followed directly by the noun object 'Monday', establishing a starting point in time. Hence, it is a Preposition.

mockTestQuestions.q: What is the part of speech of the word 'since' in: 'He left yesterday and I haven't seen him since.'?
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'since' stands alone without an object, modifying the verb phrase 'haven't seen' by indicating time. Hence, it is an Adverb.

mockTestQuestions.q: Identify the collective noun in: 'A fleet of ships was anchored at the harbor.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'fleet' is a collective noun representing a group of ships.

mockTestQuestions.q: In the sentence: 'Wow! That was a spectacular performance,' the word 'Wow!' is a/an:
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'Wow!' expresses strong, sudden emotion (admiration) and is grammatically independent. It is an Interjection.

mockTestQuestions.q: Identify the indefinite pronoun in: 'Many were called, but few were chosen.'
mockTestQuestions.sol: 'Many' and 'few' function as Indefinite Pronouns because they represent unspecified groups of people.
